content: The Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT), a pivotal study conducted under the guidance of the American Diabetes Association (ADA), compared the efficacy of multiple daily injections (MDI) with continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII). The findings demonstrated that intensive insulin therapy significantly reduced the risk of long-term complications associated with diabetes. However, this approach was also associated with an increased risk of severe hypoglycemia. The advent of insulin analogs and the development of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems have since played a critical role in reducing these risks, improving the safety and effectiveness of intensive insulin therapy.
